issues.legal_issue: Alleged diversion of a public sports facility to private or non-sporting uses presents a public-interest matter that a High Court must consider rather than dismiss summarily.
material_facts: A public stadium and its sports facilities were alleged to have been diverted to private recreational and commercial uses, including a club, a party lawn and functions.
A substantial part of the stadium property had been leased to a club for token rent, and the club had entered into arrangements with private operators.
The High Court dismissed the public interest petition in limine on the ground that no public interest was involved, without considering the alleged misuse or the related issues.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in dismissing the petition summarily because the alleged misuse implicated public interest. The appeal was allowed, the dismissal was set aside, and the petition was remanded for consideration in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: High Courts need not decide sports-administration policy or supervise stadium operations, but must protect public interest when blatant misuse of public sports facilities is brought to their notice and may direct authorities to perform their duties. No statutory provision or earlier judicial decision is expressly relied on by the Court for this ruling; the cited earlier decision was relied on by the appellant. The Court also referred to a parliamentary committee report and a draft sports policy as context.

predicates.public_interest_petition: A petitioner brought a proceeding alleging that a matter affecting the public interest required judicial consideration.
predicates.public_sports_facility_misused: A public authority or its lessee used a public sports facility in a manner inconsistent with its public sports purpose.
predicates.public_sports_facility_diverted_to_priva: A public authority or its lessee made a public sports facility available for private or commercial use.

issues.definition: When a public interest petition alleges misuse or private diversion of a public sports facility, the High Court must consider the matter and protect the public interest.

issues.legal_issue: A stadium established as a sports facility cannot be converted into a recreational club or used for private non-sporting commercial activities merely because those activities include some sport or recreation.
material_facts: The stadium property was intended for sports and sports-related activities and included sports infrastructure and open areas.
A pavilion within the stadium complex was operated as a club with facilities including a bar, restaurant and card room, while an open area was used for parties and functions.
The club entered into arrangements with private operators for management of the premises and for functions and other activities.
The Court distinguished exclusive sports stadia from multipurpose community arenas planned to accommodate public or entertainment events without impairing their sports use.
issues.conclusion: A sports complex cannot be converted into a recreational club, and a sports stadium cannot be converted or diverted to non-sporting recreational or commercial use; a club does not become a sports club merely because it offers some sports activities.
issues.legal_principle: Sports facilities created for athletes, sports persons and the public must retain their sports purpose; recreational facilities such as tennis or badminton do not make a recreational club a sports club. The Court distinguished a stadium planned as a multipurpose community arena, whose planned public-event use must not impair its sports function. No statutory provision or earlier judicial decision is expressly relied on for this principle.

predicates.exclusive_sports_stadium: A government or public authority established and designated a stadium for sports and sports-related use rather than as a planned multipurpose community arena.
predicates.converted_to_recreational_club: A public authority or its lessee turned all or part of the sports stadium into a recreational club.
predicates.used_for_private_non_sporting_commercial: A public authority or its lessee used all or part of the sports stadium for private commercial or other non-sporting activities.

issues.definition: An exclusive public sports stadium that is converted into a recreational club or used for private non-sporting commercial purposes is subject to the rule that such conversion or use is impermissible.
